ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First look at the image: this is an isosceles trapezoid ABCD, with A at the lower left, D at the lower right, B at the upper left, and C at the upper right; X is on the left leg AB, Y is on the right leg CD, and 78° is marked near D in the figure, corresponding to ∠ADY. Then reason: because Y is on CD, ∠ADY is ∠ADC, equal to 78°. The two base angles on the same base of an isosceles trapezoid are equal, so ∠DAB = ∠ADC = 78°. Also because AD ∥ BC, the interior angles on the same side along leg AB are supplementary, so ∠ABC = 180° - 78° = 102°. Finally, X is on AB, and BX is collinear with BA, therefore ∠XBC = ∠ABC = 102°.

raw_record.question_text: For isosceles trapezoid $ABCD$, $X$ and $Y$ are midpoints of the legs. Find $m\angle XBC$ if $m\angle ADY=78$.

method.method_draft: Read from the diagram that A-D is the lower base, B-C is the upper base, X lies on leg AB, and Y lies on leg CD. The marked angle is ∠ADY = 78°, and since D, Y, C are collinear, this is the same as the lower-right interior angle ∠ADC. From the text, ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid, so the two lower base angles are congruent: ∠DAB = ∠ADC = 78°. Because AD is parallel to BC, consecutive interior angles on leg AB are supplementary, so ∠ABC = 180° - 78° = 102°. Since X lies on AB, ray BX is the same direction as ray BA, hence ∠XBC = ∠ABC = 102°.
